clue.text: Mention a politician's visiting that holiday venue

indicators.note: one who visits goes into a place, so the politician's letters go inside the word for mention

parts.note: to cite something is to mention it
MP is a Member of Parliament; MP'S is the possessive, written MPS

explanation.surface: A politician turns up at a holiday spot and the visit gets mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people pitch tents on vacation is a holiday venue.

clue.text: Hit on head round end of low farm building

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the coshing word is wrapped around a letter

parts.note: to cosh someone is to club them on the head

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of low

explanation.surface: Someone is struck on the head near a lowing farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like a cow's moo here, fitting the farm scene, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter for cattle is a farm building.

clue.text: Old lady worried, entering empty manor

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the word for worried goes into the manor's letters
empty means the inside is taken away, leaving the outer letters of manor

parts.note: something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: An elderly woman frets as she walks into a deserted manor house.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for mother, it is old-fashioned British slang for one's mum, as is old lady.

clue.text: Group of players ordered hot tarts in grocer's

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Musicians order hot tarts at the grocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a containment signal but is part of the fodder for 'ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of violins, violas, cellos and basses is a group of players.

clue.text: Score unbelievable by Yorkshire's opener

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letter follows the first word

parts.note: a tall story is an unbelievable one

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, of Yorkshire's; a cricket opener is also the first batsman

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire opening batsman makes an unbelievable cricket score.
explanation.walkthrough: An opener in cricket is a batsman who starts the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running count of points, so a score.

clue.text: Material being initially engulfed in flames

indicators.note: something engulfed in a thing is swallowed up inside it, so a letter goes into the word for flames

parts.note: flames are fire

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word being

explanation.surface: A piece of material catches and is consumed by flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric or thread is material, as in natural or synthetic textile stuff.

clue.text: Quakers a source of insurance?

parts.note: the Quakers are the Religious Society of Friends, and a mutual association offering cover goes by a related name

explanation.surface: It asks whether members of the Quaker faith sell insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Quakers are formally the Religious Society of Friends; in Britain a mutual body providing cover against illness or old age has a similar name.
explanation.definitionFit: A British mutual association whose members pay in for sickness and pension benefits is a source of insurance.

clue.text: Be a bright sort, making weapon

indicators.note: as a verb, to sort is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to be a clever type and make a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like a noun (a bright sort of person), but it is the anagram signal; 'making' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the nickname of a huge German First World War howitzer, a weapon.

clue.text: Daily train

definitions.meaning: a daily newspaper; the Daily ... is a British tabloid
a fast passenger service stopping at few stations

explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a UK daily paper and a fast train making few stops.

clue.text: Register vehicle in primitive building

parts.note: a log is a record or register
a cab is a taxi, a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone registers a vehicle while living in a crude hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut of rough timber trunks is a basic, primitive building.

clue.text: Drink: steward spills one

indicators.note: spilling something lets it fall out, so the letter for one is dropped from the steward's word

parts.note: a steward serving at table is a waiter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A steward clumsily spills someone's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain tap liquid from the jug is a drink, the simplest one going.

clue.text: Improving what chef's doing, changing starter

indicators.note: the starter here is the opening letter, which is swapped for another; the starter also teases a first course

parts.note: a chef is cooking up a meal

explanation.surface: A chef improves the menu by changing the starter course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course of a meal, but it is the first letter: C becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are getting better are said, idiomatically, to be on the up.

clue.text: King once keeping rook along with old birds together

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the king's name has letters put inside it

parts.note: Henry was the name of eight English kings of the past
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A former king keeps a rook among a collection of old birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' and 'old birds' tempt a bird synonym, but rook is the chess abbreviation and old just its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding colony where herons nest together is named after those birds.

clue.text: Meet churchman in one, near front of cathedral

indicators.note: near tells us the letter from cathedral sits right beside the rest
the front of a word is its first letter, here of cathedral
the churchman is placed in the word one

parts.note: taken as written
Ven. is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Churchmen gather in one group close to the cathedral entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Ven. (Venerable) is the title given to an archdeacon.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble formally, as a council or committee does, is to meet.

clue.text: Upsets fellow dancers, perhaps, embracing your uncle? Extremely unusual

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so other letters are put inside the dancers' word

parts.note: partners on a nightclub floor could be disco mates; perhaps marks it as an example
from the British catchphrase 'Bob's your uncle', meaning there you are

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of unusual

explanation.surface: Fellow dancers hug your uncle, which is extremely unusual and upsets everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's your uncle' is a British phrase meaning 'and there you have it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discombobulate is a jokey word for confuse or disconcert, so it upsets.

clue.text: Hitchcock film, American picture set in Israel

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so the American picture goes inside the word for Israel

parts.note: Sion is a variant of Zion, the Jewish homeland, Israel
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: An American film is shot on location in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sion is an older spelling of Zion, standing for Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a 1941 thriller directed by Alfred Hitchcock.

clue.text: Where you might see New York woman with style

definitions.text: Where you might see New York

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
a way of doing something is its style

explanation.surface: A stylish woman is on display in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous avenue runs through Manhattan, a place where a visitor sees the city at its most typical.

clue.text: Radio 3 output perfect?

parts.note: BBC Radio 3 broadcasts classical music, so its output is music; a perfect thing to hear is described by this phrase

explanation.surface: A listener praises the BBC classical station's programmes as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: BBC Radio 3 is Britain's classical music station, so its output is literally music; the question mark signals the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes news or sounds that are welcome and delightful, i.e. perfect to hear.

clue.text: Liam and Sam turned out very smelly

indicators.note: turned out means made into something different, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two lads, Liam and Sam, turn out to be very smelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' only joins the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a foul vapour, so the adjective describes something with a noxious stench.

clue.text: Overnight train: it's on the track

definitions.meaning: a night train with beds for passengers
the wooden or concrete beam on which rails rest

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the railway: a train with bunks, and the crosswise beam the rails sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a night train with berths and a railway tie under the rails.

clue.text: Cake flavouring? A shortage is admitted

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so the word is goes into the word for shortage

parts.note: a need is a lack or shortage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker admits there is a shortage of flavouring for the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice-tasting seeds are one example of a flavouring used in cakes, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dish for tart

definitions.meaning: a small ovenproof pot for baking eggs and the like
an old word for a prostitute or kept woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish for tart' reads like a pie plate, but 'tart' means a loose woman, the other sense of the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword names both a small ramekin-style pot and a courtesan.

clue.text: What's 254 cm? Singularly easy answer

indicators.note: singularly asks for the singular form, so the plural ending is taken off

parts.note: 254 centimetres is 100 inches, and C is the Roman numeral 100

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what 254 centimetres is, promising an easy reply.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so 254 cm is C inches; 'Singularly' drops the ES of the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without effort is called, informally, a doddle or sure thing: an easy answer.

clue.text: Entire serving of spirit: a litre

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A litre is a whole serving of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete or whole, as in a full count, means entire.

clue.text: Transport boy, we might say, gets to school

indicators.note: what we might say out loud signals a word heard rather than read, a word for boy

parts.note: a boy is male
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A boy gets to school by some form of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets to' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway service carrying post is a means of transport for letters.

clue.text: Drunk topes in bar

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who topes, drinking heavily, ends up drunk in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: To tope is to drink heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to bar or preclude someone from asserting something is the legal verb meaning this.

clue.text: Woman beautiful in dainty clothes

indicators.note: as a verb, clothes means covers or wraps, so the words wrap the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A woman looks beautiful in dainty clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun, but it is a verb: the words 'beautiful in dainty' clothe the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female first name, so a woman.

clue.text: Cheryl's bashed front of red car

indicators.note: something bashed is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
front of points to the first letter of red

explanation.surface: Cheryl has bashed the front of her red car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an American automobile make, so a car.
